Citizen orienteering races are run in Beijing, for example the Zhongguancun sports carnival race at Xishan Forest Park (Oct 2025, 500 participants) and city-wide events registered via the Beijing Fitness mini-program.

Beijing International Dragon Boat Club, founded in 2001 starting with foreign expats, fields teams for domestic and international races (training venue and current schedule unconfirmed).

Stand-up paddleboards can be rented at the North Moat and Zhuanhe River starting piers (about 2 km routes each) from 10:00 to 21:00.

Casa Flamenco in the CBD teaches flamenco dance and guitar for all levels, taught by teachers trained in Spain and the USA.
Private teachers advertise beginner to advanced guitar lessons on The Beijinger classifieds (June 2026), and Let's School offers guitar, drum and bass classes.

No drive-through safari lies within about 30 km; Beijing Wildlife Park in Daxing has a self-drive safari section but is roughly 42 km from the centre, about an hour's drive.
No desert dunes lie near Beijing; the nearest dune fields are in the Kubuqi Desert in Inner Mongolia, several hundred kilometres west (a flight plus road transfer).
Indoor ski simulators operate in malls (SkyTechSport installation at Wangfujing; Snow51 has expanded into Beijing); simulator slopes rather than snow.
No outdoor ski slope lies within about 30 km of the centre; the nearest resorts are Nanshan (Miyun, roughly 62 km), Yunfoshan and Yuyang (about 60 km), with the Chongli resorts around 250 km away.
No ash-slope volcano suitable for boarding lies near Beijing; the nearest volcanic cones are around Datong (about 300 km, roughly 2 hours by high-speed rail).
No whitewater within the metro area; river rafting runs in the hills at Pinggu (Lishugou) and Fangshan (Shidu), roughly 70-100 km and 1.5-2 hours from the centre.
